# PDEL4 · HTML Deliverable Canvas Contract

Slice ID: PDEL4
Slice name: HTML Deliverable Canvas Contract
Status: code_complete (pending founder review for `verified`)
Authored: 2026-04-25
Author: Code (sole)
Type: Specification / contract document only — no application code,
no runtime modification, no migrations, no model calls.

This contract defines the **central canvas render contract** for
HTML deliverables generated by Nexus and approved by Steward. It
extends PDEL (Program Deliverables / Artifacts Read Model) and
PDEL3 (the canonical canvas render today) into an explicit surface
contract: how the canvas composes, how the evidence and missing-
input panel reads, how versioning binds to the Stub → Outline →
Rich promotion ladder, and how the approve / regenerate / download
actions resolve. Downstream slices PDEL5–PDEL8 implement the
deferred surfaces: export actions, the meeting-notes / workshop
materials view, the Nexus deliverable generation runtime, and the
versioning + evidence-trace write path. **No application code, no
runtime modification, no migrations, no model calls in this slice.**

---

## §A · Render modes

The deliverable canvas supports exactly **five canonical render
modes**, in canonical order. Modes are mutually exclusive; only
one renders at a time. Today the canvas implements the first
mode; the rest are documented for downstream slices.

1. **`html`** — canonical canvas render. Implemented today by
   PDEL3. The deliverable is composed into an HTML view-model
   and rendered by a server component into the center canvas.
   This is the only mode whose visual treatment is asserted by
   the present slice.
2. **`markdown`** — raw markdown view. Useful for debugging and
   for the Maestro to verify the deterministic seed. Renders the
   underlying markdown source verbatim, in a monospace block, with
   no live retrieval. Read-only in this slice.
3. **`pdf_export_later`** — deferred. PDF export pipeline lands in
   PDEL5. The mode name is reserved so the canvas can declare the
   affordance honestly without claiming the export is wired.
4. **`docx_export_later`** — deferred. DOCX export pipeline lands
   in PDEL5. Same honest-affordance treatment.
5. **`ppt_export_later`** — deferred. PPT export pipeline lands in
   PDEL5. Same honest-affordance treatment.

The canvas declares the mode list in canonical order at every
render. A mode that is not declared cannot be selected. The
canvas never claims a render mode an artifact does not declare.

---

## §B · Canvas renderer contract

The canvas renderer is a **server component by default**. It
accepts a fully-resolved view-model and renders synchronously. It
does not fetch, does not call models, does not invoke retrieval,
and does not mutate state. Side effects (Approve, Regenerate,
Download) flow through explicit server actions wired by the parent
phase route (PF2 §11), not the renderer.

The renderer composes four surface regions:

```
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Header                                                                    |
|   · program name      · deliverable code (e.g. P1.D1)                      |
|   · version chip      · file-type chip (DOC / PDF / XLS / PPT / NOTE /     |
|                          HTML / DATA)                                      |
|   · status chip       (draft · in_review · approved · stale)               |
+--------------------------------------------------+-------------------------+
|                                                  |                         |
|  Body                                            |  Evidence / missing-    |
|   · the rendered deliverable in the active mode  |  input right rail       |
|   · server-rendered, no client fetch             |    (see §C)             |
|   · honest empty states for missing seeds        |                         |
|                                                  |                         |
+--------------------------------------------------+-------------------------+
|  Footer · action bar                                                       |
|   · Approve (Steward, gated)   · Regenerate (Nexus, deferred)              |
|   · Download (HTML enabled today; PDF / DOCX / PPT deferred)               |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

- **Header** — program name, deliverable code, version chip,
  file-type chip, status chip. The header is calm: no streaming
  text, no animated counters, no agent-talk. Chips render their
  state with a single static color and a single short label.
- **Body** — the rendered deliverable in the active mode. The
  body is the only region that re-skins between modes. In `html`
  it is the composed HTML view-model. In `markdown` it is the
  raw markdown block. In the three deferred export modes the
  body renders an honest disabled affordance with the canonical
  sub-label (see §I).
- **Right rail** — evidence / missing-input panel (see §C). The
  rail is non-interactive in this slice except for the drawer
  trigger inherited from the phase canvas (PF2 §11).
- **Footer · action bar** — the three canvas actions in canonical
  order: Approve, Regenerate, Download. Each action's enabled
  state is computed from the read model; no action is rendered
  enabled when its preconditions are unmet (see §E).

The renderer accepts a fully-resolved view-model with the
following minimum shape (typed in PDEL3): `{ programId,
deliverableCode, mode, version, fileType, status, body, evidence,
missingInputs, recommendedWorkshops }`. Composition of the view-
model is the upstream caller's responsibility; the renderer never
fabricates fields that are missing from the input.

---

## §C · Evidence / missing-input panel

The right rail is the **honesty surface** of the canvas. It tells
the Maestro and the Steward what evidence the deliverable cites,
what is still missing, and which workshops would unblock each
missing input. It never pretends.

The panel composes three sections, in canonical order:

1. **Cited evidence** — a list of `E-###` IDs that resolve to
   real evidence rows. Every chip carries the row's PDEL evidence
   usability state color (NAVY / AMBER / RED / MUTED per PF2 §10).
   When no evidence is cited, the section renders the honest empty
   state copy (`"no evidence cited yet"`) — never a placeholder
   citation, never a fake `E-###` chip.
2. **Missing inputs** — deterministic from the PDEL read model.
   Each missing input is a short, named field (e.g. `"baseline
   metric — order-fill rate"`, `"primary process owner"`). The
   list is computed; it is not authored by the deliverable body.
   The panel never invents a missing input that the read model
   does not assert.
3. **Workshops that would unblock each missing input** — a small
   list mapping each missing input to one or more canonical
   workshop keys (per MW1 §I). The Maestro reads this to decide
   which session to schedule next. The mapping is deterministic;
   the panel never recommends a workshop that is not in the
   canonical workshop registry.

Blocked evidence states are called out explicitly. If the
deliverable's underlying evidence is in a `blocked` state, the
panel renders a single calm caption naming the blocker and the
gate the blocker affects. The caption never softens the blocker
into a hedge.

The right rail is **read-only in this slice**. Drawer trigger
behavior follows PF2 §11 — single-instance, 120ms fade only.
Editing of evidence rows or missing inputs is the write path that
PDEL8 lands.

---

## §D · Versioning

Every deliverable carries a `version` field. The version is bound
to the **Stub → Outline → Rich** promotion ladder defined in MW1
§J:

- **Stub** — minimal deterministic seed. Section headers and
  sentinel placeholders only. Renders as an honest skeleton; the
  body never invents content the seed does not carry.
- **Outline** — promoted from Stub when captured workshop content
  fills the outline scaffolding. The body composes the captured
  bullets, decisions, and structured fields, but does not yet
  read as a finished narrative.
- **Rich** — promoted from Outline when the captured content is
  sufficient to read as a finished deliverable. Promotion to Rich
  is deterministic per MW1 §J — no model invocation, no narrative
  invention.

The version chip in the canvas header surfaces the active tier.
Chip copy is one of `stub`, `outline`, `rich`. The chip is calm:
single static color per tier, no animation, no streaming.

**Version history is read-only in this slice.** The canvas may
display the active version, but it does not expose a history
viewer, a diff viewer, or a rollback affordance. The history
view, the diff view, and the audit-row write path land in PDEL8
(Versioning & Evidence Trace).

---

## §E · Approve / Regenerate / Download actions

The canvas footer renders three actions in canonical order.
Action semantics follow.

### Approve

- **Role** — Steward only. The Maestro and any other role render
  the affordance disabled with the canonical caption `"steward
  approval required"`.
- **Precondition** — gated on §C evidence completeness. Approve
  is enabled only when no missing inputs remain in the panel and
  no cited evidence is in a `blocked` state. Otherwise the
  affordance is disabled with a calm caption naming the failing
  precondition (e.g. `"missing 1 input · primary process
  owner"`).
- **Effect** — flips deliverable status to `approved`. The
  status chip in the header re-renders. The approval mechanism
  is the existing PDEL approval contract; **PDEL4 does not change
  it**. PDEL4 only specifies how the affordance reads in the
  canvas footer.
- **Audit** — every approve action emits an audit row tagged with
  the approving Steward, the deliverable code, and the active
  version. Audit composition is the existing PDEL contract.

### Regenerate

- **Role** — Nexus only. No human role can press Regenerate; the
  affordance reads as a Nexus-internal action. The Maestro and
  the Steward render the affordance disabled.
- **State in PDEL4** — **deferred**. Live runtime regeneration
  is documented as PDEL7 (Nexus Deliverable Generation Contract).
  In PDEL4 the action is rendered as a **disabled affordance**
  with the canonical sub-label `"deferred · live nexus runtime"`.
- **No fabricated runtime claim.** The canvas never claims
  Regenerate is wired when it is not. The disabled affordance is
  the only honest treatment.

### Download

- **State in PDEL4** — disabled in this slice except for the
  implemented `html` render. PDF / DOCX / PPT exports are
  deferred to PDEL5 (Download / Export Actions). Each deferred
  export renders as a disabled affordance with the canonical
  sub-label `"deferred · live nexus runtime"`.
- **HTML download** — enabled when the active mode is `html` and
  the body view-model is resolved. The download serializes the
  rendered HTML view-model. It does not call a model and does
  not retrieve.
- **No spoofed export.** The canvas never produces a PDF, DOCX,
  or PPT in this slice. Attempting to enable the affordance from
  the read model is a contract violation.

---

## §F · File-type chips

The header file-type chip surfaces the underlying source artifact
for the deliverable, per the AbarVa visual canon §I (DES1). The
canonical chip set is:

- **DOC** — DOCX-source artifact (e.g. uploaded charter).
- **PDF** — PDF-source artifact (e.g. signed change order).
- **XLS** — spreadsheet-source artifact (e.g. baseline metric
  table).
- **PPT** — slide-source artifact (e.g. steering committee deck).
- **NOTE** — workshop notes capture (typed / pasted / uploaded).
- **HTML** — server-rendered HTML deliverable. The implemented
  render mode in this slice.
- **DATA** — structured-data artifact (e.g. inventory readout).

`HTML` is the **implemented render mode**. The other chips
surface as **honest indicators of the underlying source artifact,
not as live exports**. A `PDF` chip on a deliverable does not
imply a live PDF export pipeline; it tells the Maestro the source
artifact is a PDF. The canvas never reuses a file-type chip to
imply a render mode the artifact does not declare.

---

## §G · Nexus generation behavior

Nexus generates deliverables only when the §C evidence
completeness check passes. If evidence is missing, Nexus refuses
with an honest message naming the missing inputs and the workshops
that would unblock them. The refusal is calm and specific; it
never hedges, never apologizes, never promises a future generation
without naming the blocker.

Refusal contract:

- The refusal names every missing input by its canonical field
  name (matching the §C panel).
- The refusal names at least one canonical workshop key per
  missing input that would unblock it.
- The refusal does not invent a deliverable body.
- The refusal does not write a placeholder `E-###` citation.
- The refusal does not promote the deliverable's version tier.

Nexus never writes `E-###` citations that do not resolve. Every
citation Nexus emits is a real evidence row in the PDEL read
model. Fabricated citations are a contract violation.

**Live runtime generation is deferred to PDEL7.** In PDEL4 the
generation behavior is documented; the runtime that performs the
generation is not wired. The canvas never claims live runtime is
active. The Regenerate affordance carries the `"deferred · live
nexus runtime"` sub-label per §E.

---

## §H · Steward approval and gate relationship

Steward approval flips deliverable status to `approved`.
Deliverables that satisfy hard-gate inputs (G1 / G2 / G3 / G4 per
the program phase workspace contract, PF2 §10) update gate
readiness on the right rail of the phase canvas.

PDEL4 does not modify gate readiness logic. Gate readiness
remains owned by S9C (Program Phase Gate Status Rendering) and PF2
(Program Phase Workspace Contract). PDEL4 only documents the
**touchpoint**: when a deliverable is approved, the gate readiness
read model recomputes and the phase canvas right rail re-renders
calmly. There is no banner, no toast, no animation.

The advance-phase affordance in PF2 remains gated on hard-gate
input completeness. A single deliverable approval does not
silently advance the phase; the Maestro is the only role that
advances the phase, and only against the gate readiness mode (PF2
§4.6).

---

## §I · No-fabrication rules

The canvas, the panel, the action bar, and Nexus generation all
share a strict no-fabrication contract. The following are
explicitly banned:

- **No fabricated dollar amounts** in any deliverable body, in any
  evidence chip caption, in any missing-input caption, in any
  workshop recommendation. Dollar amounts surface only when a
  real value-ledger row is referenced (per S9D / S9G), never as
  authored text.
- **No fabricated `E-###` citations.** Every citation must
  resolve to a real evidence row in the PDEL read model. A
  citation that does not resolve is a contract violation; the
  panel renders the honest empty state instead.
- **No live-runtime claims when runtime is not wired.** The
  canvas never asserts Regenerate is live, never asserts an
  export pipeline is live, never asserts retrieval is live in
  PDEL4. The deferred affordances carry the canonical sub-label.
- **No fake meeting notes.** The canvas never authors a
  meeting-notes body. Workshop materials surface in the meeting-
  notes view (PDEL6), not in the deliverable canvas, and never
  as fabricated capture.
- **Disabled affordances must use the canonical sub-label**
  `"deferred · live <agent> runtime"` (e.g. `"deferred · live
  nexus runtime"`). No other phrasing is acceptable for a
  deferred runtime affordance.
- **Honest empty states required** for missing evidence, missing
  inputs, and missing workshops. The canonical empty states are
  short, calm captions — not placeholder content, not skeleton
  shimmers, not "coming soon" copy.

---

## §J · Acceptance criteria

A future test slice (PDEL4-tests, not in this slice) could
verify the following assertions against a fixture deliverable.

1. The canvas declares exactly five render modes — `html`,
   `markdown`, `pdf_export_later`, `docx_export_later`,
   `ppt_export_later` — in canonical order, and identifies `html`
   as the implemented mode.
2. The renderer composes four surface regions — header, body,
   right rail, footer — and is a server component by default with
   no fetch, no model invocation, and no state mutation.
3. The right rail composes three sections in canonical order —
   cited evidence, missing inputs, workshops — and renders the
   honest empty state copy when any section is empty; no
   fabricated `E-###` chips render.
4. The version chip surfaces one of `stub`, `outline`, or `rich`,
   bound to the MW1 §J promotion ladder; version history is not
   exposed as a viewer, a diff, or a rollback in this slice.
5. The Approve action is enabled only when no missing inputs
   remain and no cited evidence is `blocked`; otherwise it is
   disabled with a calm caption naming the failing precondition,
   and Approve never bypasses the existing PDEL approval contract.
6. The Regenerate action is rendered as a disabled affordance for
   every role with the canonical sub-label `"deferred · live nexus
   runtime"`; the canvas never claims live regeneration runtime.
7. The Download action is enabled only for the `html` mode in
   this slice; PDF / DOCX / PPT downloads are disabled with the
   canonical sub-label, and the canvas never produces a PDF, DOCX,
   or PPT file in this slice.
8. The header file-type chip surfaces one of DOC / PDF / XLS /
   PPT / NOTE / HTML / DATA per DES1 §I; chips never imply a
   render mode the artifact does not declare.
9. Nexus generation refuses honestly when evidence is missing,
   naming every missing input by its canonical field name and at
   least one canonical workshop key per missing input; no
   fabricated body and no fabricated citation are emitted.
10. The contract introduces no new runtime modules; it does not
    modify Sentinel, Atlas, Nexus, Agent runtime, Source UI,
    legacy `/programs`, `mock.ts`, auth, or supabase, and it does
    not change gate readiness logic.

## §K · Future slices

- **PDEL5 · Download / Export Actions (PDF, DOCX, PPT)** — wires
  the three deferred export modes into a real export pipeline.
  Replaces the disabled affordances in §E with enabled ones once
  the export runtime is online.
- **PDEL6 · Meeting Notes / Workshop Materials View** — a
  separate render surface for typed / pasted / uploaded workshop
  materials per PF4. Notes do not render in the deliverable
  canvas; they render in their own surface, with their own
  evidence chip vocabulary.
- **PDEL7 · Nexus Deliverable Generation Contract (live
  runtime)** — replaces the deterministic seed with a
  retrieval-backed live generation runtime. Wires Regenerate as
  an enabled affordance and removes the `"deferred · live nexus
  runtime"` sub-label.
- **PDEL8 · Versioning & Evidence Trace (write path + history
  view)** — adds the version-history viewer, the diff viewer, the
  rollback affordance, and the audit-row write path for evidence
  trace. Replaces the read-only version treatment in §D.
